We evaluated the workflow on optical transmittance spectra from 203 epitaxial β-Ga2O3 films grown during a previously reported self-driving thin-film growth campaign. The predefined optical analysis script returned Urbach energy, an optical-quality metric, for 183 spectra and failed for 20. The agent retained those 183 values and evaluated 20 exception cases, recovering 16 through bounded parameter adjustments and returning NaN for 4 when the spectral evidence did not support a reliable Urbach tail. The audit records captured spectral features, parameter changes, and rationale for each decision. These results demonstrate autonomous scientific exception handling by an LLM agent while leaving quantitative property extraction to deterministic numerical analysis. 1. We collected 32 research tasks from domain experts, with eight tasks in each of four catalysis domains (Fig. 2B, note 4 of the supplementary text, and table S8). Together, these tasks formed a test suite for general catalysis research spanning electrocatalysis, electrochemical materials and testing, photocatalysis and thermal catalysis. Electrocatalysis tasks covered the oxygen evolution, hydrogen evolution, urea oxidation and ethanol oxidation reactions. Electrodes tasks covered cyclic voltammetry, impedance spectroscopy and ion-storage measurements. Photocatalysis tasks addressed H2 and H2O2 production and selective oxidation, whereas thermal-catalysis tasks focused on selective hydrogenation. Rather than repeating a canonical protocol, the suite required different combinations of sample synthesis, structural characterization, reaction testing and product analysis. A representative task asks the agent to improve urea conversion and target-product yield for Ni-based catalysts in alkaline urea oxidation. The agent must design and dispatch an experiment to robotic Laboratory 303 and return the resulting task identifier. Model construction from a dimensionally reduced EFT We illustrate the three-dimensional EFT workflow using the xSM implemented in the DRalgo source file xsm_test.m, provided in the PTagent repository. This file is adapted from the official DRalgo xSM example [25] to describe a specific Z2-symmetric model and a well-defined dimensional-reduction setup. In particular, the singlet interactions that are odd under the Z2 symmetry are removed, and the original tutorial’s multiple reduction paths are restricted to a single setup that retains both the Higgs and singlet scalar fields in the three-dimensional theory. The adapted file also specifies the Standard Model hypercharges and employs a consistent mass-basis treatment, including the rotation of interaction tensors required for higher-order effective-potential calculations. Starting from this DRalgo source, PTagent identifies the relevant model information and invokes DRalgo to obtain the matched three-dimensional effective theory. The calculation can be initiated with the following instruction. $ptagent Use xsm_test.m to generate a PhaseTracer model with the default scale policy.
